title: Bounded flat test pairs detect isomorphisms of exact coproduct-preserving bifunctors
statement:
Let $U,V$ be schemes, let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring, and use $D_U=D(U_{\Et},\Lambda)$ and $D_V=D(V_{\Et},\Lambda)$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Write $Q_U,Q_V$ for localization from cochain complexes to these derived categories. Let $\mathcal T$ be a triangulated category [def-weil-triangulated-category] with countable coproducts [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Let $A,B:D_U\times D_V\to\mathcal T$ be bifunctors exact and preserving countable coproducts separately in each variable. Give each one-variable functor its specified exact-functor shift comparisons. Let $\alpha:A\to B$ be a natural transformation such that, with either input fixed and the other denoted $C$, its components satisfy
$$\chi_{B,m,C}\alpha_{C[m]}=\alpha_C[m]\chi_{A,m,C}\quad(m\in\mathbf Z),\qquad \chi_{A,m,C}:A(C[m])\xrightarrow{\sim}A(C)[m],$$
and likewise for $B$. Suppose $\alpha_{Q_UP^\bullet,Q_VR^\bullet}$ is an isomorphism for every bounded cochain complex $P^\bullet$ of flat $\Lambda_U$-module sheaves [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] and every bounded cochain complex $R^\bullet$ of $\Lambda_V$-module sheaves. Here bounded means that the terms vanish outside some finite interval; its bounds can depend on the complex, and zero complexes are included. Then $\alpha_{E,F}$ is an isomorphism for every $E\in D_U$ and $F\in D_V$, with no boundedness hypothesis.

proof.text: Fix either input and call the resulting functors $G,H$ and transformation $\beta:G\to H$. For a sequence $(C_n,u_n)$ in the other derived category put $S=\bigoplus_n C_n$, with coprojections $i_n$, and $s i_n=i_{n+1}u_n$ [def-kun-truncations]. By preservation of countable coproducts, $G(S)$ and $H(S)$ are coproducts with coprojections $G(i_n)$ and $H(i_n)$. Naturality gives $\beta_S G(i_n)=H(i_n)\beta_{C_n}$. If every $\beta_{C_n}$ is invertible, the coproduct universal property gives $v:H(S)\to G(S)$ with $vH(i_n)=G(i_n)\beta_{C_n}^{-1}$. Restricting $v\beta_S$ and $\beta_S v$ to all coprojections proves that both are identities. Thus $\beta_S$ is invertible. Exactness includes additivity [def-weil-triangulated-category], so $G(1-s)=1-G(s)$ and likewise for $H$.

Suppose $C$ is any homotopy colimit, with chosen telescope triangle $S\xrightarrow{1-s}S\xrightarrow{p}C\xrightarrow{q}S[1]$. The exact functors $G,H$ send this to distinguished triangles, whose last arrows are $\chi_{G,1,S}G(q)$ and $\chi_{H,1,S}H(q)$; these are the image telescope triangles described by [lem-kun-functor-preserves-hocolim]. Naturality at $1-s,p,q$ gives the first two squares for $(\beta_S,\beta_S,\beta_C)$ and the equation $\beta_{S[1]}G(q)=H(q)\beta_C$. The assumed shift equation gives $\chi_{H,1,S}\beta_{S[1]}=\beta_S[1]\chi_{G,1,S}$, so also
$$\beta_S[1]\chi_{G,1,S}G(q)=\chi_{H,1,S}H(q)\beta_C.$$
Thus these three specified components form a morphism of distinguished triangles. If all $\beta_{C_n}$ are invertible, Step 1 makes its first two components invertible, and [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso] makes $\beta_C$ invertible. This proves closure under sequential homotopy colimits in either input. No choice of a functor on cone objects is needed.

Let $P^\bullet$ be a bounded-above complex of flat $\Lambda_U$-module sheaves and $R^\bullet$ a bounded-above complex of $\Lambda_V$-module sheaves, with upper term bounds $b,c\in\mathbf Z$. For $n,m\ge0$ put $P_n=\sigma_{\ge-n}P$ and $R_m=\sigma_{\ge-m}R$ [def-kun-truncations]. These are subcomplexes, with inclusion transition maps, supported in $[-n,b]$ and $[-m,c]$. Empty intervals give zero complexes. All terms of $P_n$ are flat, since they are terms of $P$ or zero (tensoring with zero is the zero exact functor). By the test-pair hypothesis $\alpha_{Q_UP_n,Q_VR_m}$ is invertible for every $n,m$. In each fixed degree $r$, once $m\ge\max(0,-r)$ the $r$-th term of $R_m$ and all later transition maps are $R^r$ and its identity. The degreewise colimit is therefore $R$, with its original differential. Apply [lem-kun-complex-colimit-hocolim] to exhibit $Q_VR$ as the homotopy colimit of $(Q_VR_m)$. For each fixed $n$, Step 2 in the second input gives invertibility of $\alpha_{Q_UP_n,Q_VR}$.

For the same $P,R$, in each degree $r$ the terms $(P_n)^r$ stabilize to $P^r$ for $n\ge\max(0,-r)$, with identity transition maps; their differentials are eventually those of $P$. Hence the degreewise colimit of $(P_n)$ is $P$ [def-kun-truncations]. By [lem-kun-complex-colimit-hocolim], $Q_UP$ is a homotopy colimit of $(Q_UP_n)$. Keeping $Q_VR$ fixed, Step 2 and the invertibility obtained in Step 3 prove $\alpha_{Q_UP,Q_VR}$ invertible for every bounded-above flat $P$ and every bounded-above $R$.

Now let $C^\bullet,D^\bullet$ be arbitrary complexes of $\Lambda_U$- and $\Lambda_V$-module sheaves whose terms vanish above some bounds $b,c$. Apply [lem-kun-bounded-flat-replacement] to $C$, with bound $b$, obtaining a bounded-above flat complex $P$ and a quasi-isomorphism $t:P\to C$. Localization makes $Q_U(t)$ invertible [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Step 4 applies to $(P,D)$. Naturality in the first input gives
$$\alpha_{Q_UC,Q_VD}\,A(Q_Ut,1)=B(Q_Ut,1)\,\alpha_{Q_UP,Q_VD}.$$
Both functors carry the isomorphism $(Q_Ut,1)$ to isomorphisms (apply them to its inverse), so this equality proves $\alpha_{Q_UC,Q_VD}$ invertible. Flat replacement has been used only in the first variable, and no flatness or finite Tor dimension is imposed on $D$.

Take arbitrary $E\in D_U$ and $F\in D_V$, represented by complexes $C,D$ using [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Set $E_n=\tau_{\le n}E$, $F_m=\tau_{\le m}F$ for $n,m\ge0$. By [def-kun-truncations] these are represented by the good truncations of $C,D$, with zero terms above $n,m$, respectively. Step 5 proves $\alpha_{E_n,F_m}$ invertible for every $n,m$. By [lem-kun-hocolim-truncations], a homotopy colimit of $(F_m)$ is isomorphic to $F$. Fix $n$ and apply Step 2 in the second input to that telescope; naturality at the resulting isomorphism with $F$ proves $\alpha_{E_n,F}$ invertible. This last transport is conjugation by the two functors' images of the isomorphism, as in Step 5.

By [lem-kun-hocolim-truncations], a homotopy colimit of $(E_n)$ is isomorphic to $E$. Keep the original arbitrary $F$ fixed and use the invertible components $\alpha_{E_n,F}$ from Step 6. Step 2 in the first input proves invertibility at this telescope, and naturality at its isomorphism with $E$ gives invertibility of $\alpha_{E,F}$. Both sequences are indexed by the natural numbers; only the assumed countable coproducts, exactness in each variable, and the $m=1$ instance of the stipulated shift compatibility were used.
